newsitem.title: HONG KONG: "Speechless" accountant slams HK 97/98 budget.
newsitem.headline: "Speechless" accountant slams HK 97/98 budget.

text.p: One of Hong Kong's most prominent tax accountants said he was "speechless" at Financial Secretary Donald Tsang's failure to do more to reduce the territory's surplus and reserves in the 1997/98 budget delivered on Wednesday.

"It's really left me speechless. I'm still bemused at the boldness of his ability to stand up and tell us he's going to accumulate HK$90 billion in surplus over the next four years," said Marshall Byres, chairman of tax services at Ernst & Young in Hong Kong.

In the budget straddling the handover on July 1, when Hong Kong becomes a Special Administrative Region (SAR) of China, Tsang estimated a surplus of HK$15.1 billion at March 31, rising to HK$31.7 billion at March 31, 1998.
The budget was designed by a committee under the auspices of the Sino-British Joint Liaison Group overseeing the handover.

Tsang also forecast a combined budget surplus of HK$58.9 billion for the three fiscal years 1998/99, 1999/2000 and 2000/01 but warned of huge capital expenditures in the same period on Hong Kong's railway system.
"However, it would be imprudent of me not to warn this Council of the huge capital investments which may be needed during this period," Tsang told the Legislative Council.

"Over the past three years, 1994/95 to 1996/97, we have contributed HK$49 billion to the Airport Authority and to the Mass Transit Railway Corporation to help finance the construction of the airport and the airport railway," he said.
"The SAR government may well need to contribute a similar sum between 1998 and 2001 towards the construction of the high-priority projects under the Railway Development Strategy."
Byres described these statements as a pretense.
"He's used this as a pretense, is the only word I can use, as the rationale for keeping all this money, which is clearly what Beijing consultants who were in this group wanted him to do," Byres said.

"I'm reading between the lines that they did not want him to give any tax cuts, they wanted him to build up more cash and he's used the prospect of maybe having to fund -- and it is an important project, the railway development project -- out of recurrent revenues as the need for keeping this HK$90 billion there," Byres said.
Tsang said fiscal reserves would rise to HK$330 billion, including the SAR Land Fund, by the time of the handover.
